source.quote: iFi audio's own product page for the ZEN DAC 3, read 2026-11-24: « PCM data to 32-bit/768kHz, DSD up to DSD512 and single and double speed DXD. Thanks to the Burr-Brown DAC chip's four-channel True Native design, PCM and DSD take separate pathways - this enables DSD, as well as PCM, to remain 'bit-perfect' in its native form right through to analogue conversion. »

facts.chip: A « Burr-Brown DAC chip » with a « four-channel True Native design ». The maker names the vendor and the design and not a part number, so none is invented.

_the_first_level_3_fact_a_maker_gave_thi: dsd_direct AND dsd_reconverted_to_pcm, both from one sentence, and it is explicit where Weiss's was not: « PCM and DSD take separate pathways - this enables DSD, as well as PCM, to remain 'bit-perfect' in its native form RIGHT THROUGH TO ANALOGUE CONVERSION ». That is exactly what dsd_direct asks - does the stream reach conversion unfiltered - and « separate pathways » answers dsd_reconverted_to_pcm in the same breath. Compare weiss/dac204, where « can also convert DSD audio to PCM and offers a digital output in AES/EBU format » was refused because it could be read two ways. This one cannot. The difference is that iFi names the destination: analogue conversion. Note what it does NOT establish: `correctable`. That is computed from dsd_direct on every record here, so it is not asserted - see the registry's note that a stored derivation is a second place to get one fact wrong.
_only_usb: The page read gives no second digital input and no per-input split, so only usb is recorded, with the device-level figures it states.
